newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. congressman sees no permanent MFN for China.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressman sees no permanent MFN for China.

text.p: China is unlikely to gain permanent Most Favoured Nation (MFN) status this year, U.S. congressman Jim Kolbe said on Tuesday.
The Arizona Republican told reporters that the return of Hong Kong to China on July 1 would probably delay any move by the United States to grant Beijing that status this year.
"I do not believe this year we will grant permanent MFN status to China," he told a news conference.
President Bill Clinton would have to certify the move in June, the same month as the transfer of power for the British colony. China recovers sovereignty at midnight on June 30.
"We want to monitor Hong Kong for a year before we make any change," Kolbe said.
China has been pushing for for the United States to end its annual review before renewing MFN status to Beijing.
Kolbe is leading a group of 22 congressmen to China, where they are meeting with Chinese officials including President Jiang Zemin.
